bundle.prompt:
Below is a passage from teaching material for a college course. Read it as a student of that course would, at the level it is taught, and check it for errors of fact or concept.
Raise a concern of one of two kinds. "wrong": the passage states or teaches something false at this level. "clarify": the passage is correct as meant, but a few added or changed words would remove a likely misreading (for example, by naming the condition it assumes).
Do not raise exceptions or special cases beyond what the passage is about, and nothing about style or emphasis. For each concern copy the exact words at issue, and give the words to put in their place: for "clarify", the smallest edit that keeps the meaning.
The text around the passage is given so you can read it in place; raise concerns only about words in the PASSAGE itself.
If the passage refers to something that is not shown (a numbered question, a figure, another section), do not guess what it says, and raise nothing about it.
Reply with JSON only, exactly this shape: {"nonce": "dddb529ad8b78ef5", "concerns": [{"kind": "wrong" | "clarify", "text": "exact words", "problem": "...", "suggestion": "the words to put in their place"}]} — an empty list if there is nothing to raise.

TEXT THE PASSAGE REFERS TO (context only)
Q 9: Write the equilibrium constant expression for the decomposition of solid calcium carbonate,
$\ce{CaCO3(s) <=> CaO(s) + CO2(g)}$. *(Objective 4)*

TEXT BEFORE THE PASSAGE (context only)
Answer 9: Both solids have an activity of one and are omitted, leaving only the gas:
$$K = [\ce{CO2}]$$

Q 10: For the reaction in Q9, a student adds more solid $\ce{CaCO3}$ to the sealed vessel and predicts
that more $\ce{CO2}$ will form. Evaluate the prediction. *(Objective 4)*

TEXT AFTER THE PASSAGE (context only)
Q 11: A reaction has $K = 4.0$ at $T = 298\ \text{K}$. Using $R = 8.314\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$,
calculate the standard Gibbs energy change. *(Objective 5)*

PASSAGE (Answer 10)
The prediction is wrong. A pure solid has an activity of one regardless of how much is present, so
it does not appear in the expression. Neither $K$ nor the equilibrium partial pressure of
$\ce{CO2}$ changes. Adding more solid changes only the amount of solid present.
